the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Take r in R with s(r) = u and t(r) = u'. If u' were a specialization of u, schemes-lemma-quasi-compact-closed gives a nontrivial specialization r to r' with s(r') = u'; setting u'' = t(r') one has u'' different from u' because the fibres of a finite morphism have no specializations. Iterating produces an infinite chain of specializations u to u' to u'' and so on inside the orbit t(s^{-1}({u})), contradicting finiteness of the orbit, since s, t are finite. (source lines 2971-2984)
